title: Compare Your PrEP Options
intro: Here's a side-by-side look at the three PrEP options available today. Each one is highly effective — the best choice is the one that fits your life.

categories.label: How You Take It
categories.injectable_2mo: Injection into the buttock muscle by your provider
categories.injectable_6mo: Small injection under the skin in the belly area by your provider

categories.label: Where
categories.injectable_2mo: At your provider's office or clinic
categories.injectable_6mo: At your provider's office or clinic

categories.label: Effectiveness
categories.oral: Over 99% when taken daily as directed
categories.injectable_2mo: Shown to be more effective than daily pills in clinical studies
categories.injectable_6mo: 96% reduction in HIV risk in clinical trials — highly effective

categories.label: Common Side Effects
categories.oral: Mild nausea, headache, or stomach upset when starting — usually goes away in a few weeks
categories.injectable_2mo: Soreness, swelling, or tenderness at the injection site — usually mild and temporary
categories.injectable_6mo: Small bump or nodule under the skin at the injection site — usually painless and temporary

categories.label: Getting Started
categories.oral: HIV test, kidney labs, prescription from provider. Protection builds up in about 7-21 days depending on type of exposure.
categories.injectable_2mo: HIV test, 1 month of daily oral lead-in tablets, then first injection. Second injection 1 month later, then every 2 months.
categories.injectable_6mo: HIV test, 2 oral loading tablets on Day 1, 1 tablet on Day 2, then first injection at Day 28. Next injection in 6 months.

categories.label: Stopping
categories.oral: Easy to stop — protection fades within days. Simple to restart later.
categories.injectable_2mo: Medicine stays in your body 12+ months after last injection. Must use other protection during this tail period.
categories.injectable_6mo: Medicine stays in your body for an extended period. Must work with your provider on a transition plan for continued protection.

categories.label: Privacy
categories.oral: Requires having pills at home. Could be seen by others in your household.
categories.injectable_2mo: No pills at home. Only your provider's office knows about your visits.
categories.injectable_6mo: No pills at home (after the brief oral loading). Only your provider's office knows about your visits.

categories.label: Clinic Visits
categories.oral: Every 3 months for HIV testing and prescription refills
categories.injectable_2mo: Every 2 months for your injection (includes HIV testing)
categories.injectable_6mo: Every 6 months for your injection (includes HIV testing)

categories.label: Drug Interactions
categories.oral: Few drug interactions. Tell your provider about all medications.
categories.injectable_2mo: Few drug interactions. Tell your provider about all medications.
categories.injectable_6mo: Some important interactions — certain seizure medications and St. John's wort can reduce effectiveness. Tell your provider about everything you take.

bestFor.title: The daily pill might be best if...
points: You're comfortable taking a pill every day
You like being in control of your prevention at home
You want the flexibility to easily start and stop PrEP
You prefer not to get injections
You want the option with the longest track record
You'd like access to a generic or lower-cost version

bestFor.title: The 2-month injection might be best if...
points: You don't want to remember a daily pill
You're okay with getting a shot in the buttock every 2 months
You're comfortable with regular clinic visits
You want the option that was shown to be more effective than pills in studies
Privacy is important to you — no pills at home
You're okay with the commitment and understand the long tail when stopping

bestFor.title: The 6-month injection might be best if...
points: You want the fewest possible appointments and doses
You're okay with a small shot under the skin in the belly area
You prefer not to think about HIV prevention on a daily or even monthly basis
You want a highly effective newer option
Privacy matters — no pills at home after the initial loading phase
You don't take medications that interact with lenacapavir (like St. John's wort or certain seizure medications)
